item.description: Compare punchcard and electronic knitting machines. Learn the pros, cons, and key differences to choose the best machine for your knitting projects.

item.title: Copy a Store-Bought Sweater with Your Knitting Machine
item.description: Love a sweater you spotted in the store or your closet? Before you try to copy it on your knitting machine, ask these three essential questions. This tip walks you through how to evaluate, adapt, and decide if it’s worth the effort — or better left admired.

item.title: What You’ll Find Inside a Knit It Now Classroom
item.description: Find everything you need for machine knitting — patterns, tutorials, and courses — grouped by topic in Knit It Now Classrooms.

item.title: DesignaKnit and manual machines (LK-150, TH160, KX350)
item.description: DesignaKnit is powerful software for the serious machine knitter. It is designed to interface directly with electronic machines, but can also be used with any machine, manual, punchcard or non-working electronic machines.

item.title: DesignaKnit Q&A
item.description: Straight answers to the most common DesignaKnit questions for machine knitters who are deciding if it’s worth it, plus where to get step-by-step training inside LearnDesignaKnit.com’s All Access Pass.

item.title: You Can Do This Too: Cheryl’s Lotus Lace Story
item.description: Cheryl’s Lotus Lace sweater proves what’s possible when you take a Machine Knit-able and make it your own. By pairing it with the Radiant Eyelet Lace stitch, she created a one-of-a-kind garment on her Silver Reed 860. You can do this too—choose a design, pick a stitch you love, and let your creativity shine.

item.title: What weight of yarn should I use?
item.description: Casting on shouldn’t feel impossible. If your machine refuses to cooperate, the culprit may be your yarn weight — not your skills. Learn why terms like “4-ply” can be confusing, how to match yarns to your machine, and simple fixes to avoid frustration.

item.title: latch tool
item.description: Feeling clumsy with a latch tool? You are not alone. Like writing with a pencil, skill comes with practice. Here’s how to hold, control, and use it for cleaner, more confident knitting results.
